title: Time
description: Hours worked, each tied to the work it was for, and invoices made from them. A client company says who bills it, its rate, terms and whether HST is charged.

types.title: Time entry
types.description: Time spent on one piece of work on one day, as hours or as a block from a start to an end. A planned block is time set aside, not yet worked: it counts toward nothing and is never invoiced until the owner confirms it (logged). The title says what was done in a few words; the note says more. Make it part of the work it was for (a project or task); the client is the company that work involves.

date.description: The day the work was done.

hours.description: Hours spent, e.g. 1.5. When start and end are both given, the hours are the time between them.

start.description: When the block of work began, for an entry drawn on the calendar.

end.description: When the block of work ended.

billable.description: Whether it goes on an invoice.

rate.description: An hourly rate for this entry only, when it is not the client's.

types.title: Routine
types.description: A block that repeats: the same hours on the same days of the week, like dinner from 17:00 to 19:00 every day. Nothing is stored for a day: the calendar draws it where it falls. Made part of a piece of work, each day it falls on is planned time for that work, which the owner confirms as it happened; one that is part of nothing only holds the time.

from_time.description: When it begins each day, as 17:00, in Toronto.

to_time.description: When it ends each day, as 19:00.

days.description: The days of the week it falls on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday. Every day when left out.

starts.description: The first day it falls on. From when it was made when left out.

until.description: The last day it falls on, when it ends.

skip.description: Days it does not fall on after all, as 2026-10-15.

moved.description: Days it falls at other hours: each day with its from and to, as {"2026-10-15": ["18:00", "20:00"]}.

done.description: Days of work the owner has confirmed: each made a time entry, and is no longer drawn from the routine.

types.title: Invoice
types.description: A bill to a client for time entries, kept as a document: its note is the invoice as sent, fixed when made. Read, print or share it as any document.

billed_by.description: The company or person the invoice is from.

period_from.description: The first day of the work billed.

period_to.description: The last day of the work billed.

paid.description: What has been paid so far.

paid_on.description: The day of the last payment.

payments.description: Each payment received: date, amount and method (e-Transfer, EFT, cheque, card).

relations.title: bills
relations.description: The invoice bills this time entry.

rate.description: Hourly rate billed to this client.

terms_days.description: Days until an invoice is due.

hst.description: Whether 13% HST is charged to this client.

billed_by.description: Id of the company or person who bills this client, e.g. Aperture Design Tools Inc.

hst_number.description: Its own HST number, when it bills.

payment.description: How to pay, as it goes on invoices: one way per line, e.g. "Interac e-Transfer to pay@example.com (autodeposit)" and "EFT: institution 004, transit 12345, account 1234567".

hst_number.description: HST number, when they bill as a sole proprietor.

payment.description: How to pay, as it goes on invoices: one way per line, e.g. "Interac e-Transfer to pay@example.com (autodeposit)" and "EFT: institution 004, transit 12345, account 1234567".

rules.say: "{title}" is a routine: only a person confirms a day of it, on the Time screen. Its days wait there under To confirm.
"{title}" is planned time: only a person confirms that it happened, on the Time screen. It waits there under To confirm.
"{title}" already has that number from the same biller: invoice numbers are not reused.
